name: list_companions
description: List the owner's live Minecraft companions (name + id). Call this first to see who you can drive.

name: create_companion
description: Summon a new companion into the world by name (3–16 letters, digits, or underscore). It arrives in a moment; call list_companions to confirm, then drive it directly — no 'take control' step.

name.description: The new companion's name (3–16 letters, digits, or underscore).

name: delete_companion
description: Permanently dismiss a companion — it drops its inventory, armor and accessories and is gone for good. Takes its name or id.

companion.description: Which companion to dismiss — its name or id (see list_companions).

name: get_events
description: Long-poll the companion's inbox: returns the moment something urgent arrives (the owner speaking to it shows up as a <query>; world happenings as <event>s), or whatever accumulated once wait_seconds runs out. Events are consumed on read and nothing is lost between calls — call this about every 2 seconds while you drive the companion.

companion.description: Which companion to act with — its name or id (see list_companions).

wait_seconds.description: How long to wait for something urgent before returning, in seconds (0–50, default 2). 0 = return at once. Leave it unset for the normal drive loop; raise it only to park and wait for the owner.

name: say
description: Speak as the companion: the text appears in-game as its chat line, speech bubble, and voice (if one is bound). Use it to answer the owner's <query> events and to narrate what you are doing. Consecutive calls queue up and play in order.

companion.description: Which companion to act with — its name or id (see list_companions).

text.description: What the companion says out loud.

name: lua
description: Runs a Lua 5.2 program that acts through your API, and returns one receipt when it ends. This is how you do anything in the world: every function is listed in <api>. - Every API function is written in full, `namespace.group.verb(objects..., {option = value})`: Numen's own are under numen (`numen.scan.blocks("iron_ore", {radius = 12})`, `numen.work.dig({x = 120, y = 12, z = -35})`), a mod's under …

companion.description: Which companion to act with — its name or id (see list_companions).

name: skill
description: Loads a skill — the detailed workflow for one kind of task — and returns its instructions as this call's result. - <available_skills> in the system prompt lists each skill and what it is for. When a task you are asked to do matches one, load it before you start on the task, then follow it. - A loaded skill is a <skill_content name="…"> block in the conversation, whether this tool or your owner's …

skill.description: The skill's name, as <available_skills> lists it.

file.description: Relative path of a supporting file the skill's text names, e.g. references/baroque.md. Omit to load the skill's own text.

page.description: Which page of a long text. Omit for the first.

companion.description: Which companion to act with — its name or id (see list_companions).

name: todo
description: Writes down your plan for work of several physical phases; your owner sees it as a checklist. Each call gives the whole plan and replaces the one before. - Write it before the first physical step, and again right after each verified result to mark the finished step [x] and move exactly one step to [>]. While work remains exactly one step is [>]. - Skip it for single actions and chat. - Never mark…

items.description: The whole plan, one string per step in order, each starting with its mark: [ ] to do, [>] doing now, [x] done, [-] dropped.

companion.description: Which companion to act with — its name or id (see list_companions).

name: memory
description: Keeps your own notes, which outlive this session; their index comes to you as <memory> every turn. - command "remember" writes one note: description is the line you will see in <memory>, the fact itself ("main base -340,68,120"), not a label; name is its handle (writing a name again replaces that note); content is a longer body, only when there is more worth reading later. - command "recall" read…

command.description: What to do: remember, recall or forget.

name.description: The note's handle, short kebab-case like main-base. remember: omit it to get the next free note-1, note-2, …; recall and forget: the name exactly as <memory> lists it.

description.description: remember: the one line you will see in <memory>.

type.description: remember: owner = the owner's habits and wishes, world = places and things you have seen, lesson = something you tried that did not work. Omit to file it as world.

content.description: remember: a longer body, read back with recall. Omit to keep just the line.

page.description: recall: which page of a long body. Omit for the first.

companion.description: Which companion to act with — its name or id (see list_companions).
